# Genjutsu Studio (https://genjutsu-trends.com/)

> Make viral AI video trends with your own photos, in the browser. Pick a trend, upload a photo for each part, and Higgsfield's Genjutsu model puts you in the scene. Pay per video, no subscription, no app.

Last updated: 2026-10-28. Independent site: not affiliated with or endorsed by Higgsfield AI.

## Pricing
- From $2.50 per video (Budget mode / Genjutsu Light, 480p). Premium mode and 720p/1080p cost more.
- 100 credits = $1, credits never expire, failed or blocked renders are refunded automatically.
- Full price list: https://genjutsu-trends.com/pricing/

## Trends

### White Chicks: A Thousand Miles Car Scene
URL: https://genjutsu-trends.com/trends/white-chicks/
Facts: 2 photos (Person on the left, Person on the right); horizontal MP4; Budget mode (Genjutsu Light): 15 s from $3.25; Premium: full 19 s scene from $10.07. Also called: White Chicks car scene, A Thousand Miles AI trend, Terry Crews car meme.

In the 2004 comedy White Chicks, Terry Crews' character Latrell sings Vanessa Carlton's "A Thousand Miles" in his car, and the scene has been a meme for twenty years. In 2026 AI face swaps made it blow up again, peaking during the World Cup: people swap in themselves, their friends or their favorite players and post it to TikTok, Reels and Shorts. Most face swap apps paste a flat face over the clip. Genjutsu works differently. It keeps the original motion, camera move and timing and rebuilds the characters from your photos, so the car lighting and every head turn match.

How to make it:
1. Open this page: The White Chicks car scene and the prompt are already loaded. You don't need to find the clip or a CapCut template.
2. Add two photos: Add one photo for the person on the left (passenger seat) and one for the person on the right (Terry Crews' seat, the driver). Use clear, front-facing, well-lit photos with one face each.
3. Keep 480p: 480p is the default: it's the cheapest and looks fine on TikTok, Reels and Shorts. Pick 720p or 1080p for a sharper video.
4. Click Generate: You'll see the exact price first. The video renders in a few minutes, and you can close the tab and come back.
5. Download and post: Download the MP4 and post it. Add "A Thousand Miles" in the app you post with for the full meme.

Questions:
- Q: How do I make the White Chicks AI video?
  A: Open this page. The White Chicks car scene (the "A Thousand Miles" singalong) is already loaded. Add one clear photo for the person on the left and one for the person on the right, then click Generate. Your video is ready in a few minutes.
- Q: Is the White Chicks AI face swap free?
  A: There's no subscription and no monthly plan. You buy a one-time credit pack and pay only for the videos you make. The exact price shows before you click Generate.
- Q: How much does the White Chicks AI video cost?
  A: In Budget mode (Genjutsu Light), the 15-second version at 480p costs 325 credits (about $3.25). Premium mode renders the full 19-second clip for 1,007 credits (about $10.07). 720p and 1080p are sharper and cost more. No subscription.
- Q: Is there a White Chicks AI template without CapCut?
  A: Yes. The scene is preloaded right here in the browser, on phone or desktop.
- Q: What photos work best?
  A: Clear, front-facing, well-lit photos of one person each. Avoid sunglasses, heavy shadows and group photos. Only use photos of people who agreed to be in the video.
- Q: Can I use a different scene?
  A: Yes. Use the Custom trend page to upload any MP4 between 4 and 30 seconds with your own photos and prompt.
- Q: Do I need to download an app?
  A: No. Everything runs in your browser, on a phone or a computer. Sign in with your email (we send a 6-digit code) and you're ready.
- Q: How long does it take?
  A: Usually a few minutes. You can close the tab: the video keeps rendering, it appears under "My videos" and we email you when it's ready.
- Q: What's the difference between Budget mode (Genjutsu Light) and Premium mode?
  A: Budget uses the Genjutsu Light model: fast, much cheaper, and it renders up to 15 seconds of the scene. Premium uses the full Genjutsu model: it renders the full scene with more detail, and takes a bit longer.
- Q: Which resolution should I pick?
  A: 480p is the default and looks fine on TikTok, Reels and Shorts. 720p and 1080p are sharper and cost more; the price updates as you switch.

  A: If the render fails or is blocked by the automatic content check, your credits are refunded automatically. A finished video can't be refunded, because the render has already been paid for, so use a clear, well-lit photo for the best result.
